evidence: The original sourceValuesFor did `return values, true` inside the first matching column, while countFindings sums rows across every contributing table; 7560ea1 unions across all matching columns and adds TestSourceValuesForAggregatesAcrossTables.
guidance_note: When a new helper reads the same mapping a sibling check already reads (countFindings sums across tables), make the helper aggregate the same way, and test the multi-table case before opening the PR.

evidence: The comment said 'Validate guarantees at most one column maps to a given target', but Validate's duplicate check is per table. 7560ea1 removed that sentence along with the first-match logic.
guidance_note: Before writing a comment that says another component guarantees something, check that component's actual scope (here, a per-table check), not the scope you assumed.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 7560ea1 changed only sourceValuesFor and its test, while VerifyCandidate's preamble is unchanged pre-review code. The pushback holds because RebuildCandidate validates through Apply, but citing single-enforcer for calling the same Validate function is inapt, and the packet does not confirm the agent's claim that an unknown target becomes an expected-vs-0 finding (the loop ranges over conservationCollections).
guidance_note: When pushing back with a mechanical claim ('an unknown target is reported as expected-vs-0'), point to the line that proves it; in this packet the loop shown ranges only over conservationCollections.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 7560ea1 did not touch rank.go, so the Valid doc comment dates from the original commit. It did overclaim that Midpoint/Before/After require Valid inputs, even though those functions accept an empty sentinel bound.
guidance_note: When a doc comment says a new predicate is 'exactly the precondition' of existing functions, read those functions' signatures first; here they accept an empty sentinel.

evidence: This is a verbatim duplicate of F3 posted in the same round, and it is a false positive for the same reason: 7560ea1 did not touch VerifyCandidate. This duplicates F4. The rank.go doc comment comes from the original commit, and 7560ea1 did not touch it.

narrative: Round 0 found a real first-match bug in sourceValuesFor plus the stale comment that justified it, and the fix in 7560ea1 was complete. All six round-1 findings were raised against 7560ea1 but concern code that predates it (VerifyCandidate's preamble and rank.Valid); Copilot posted each one twice. guidance_observations: Round 1's reviewer posted three findings twice each; the agent answered every copy separately instead of linking the duplicates to one reply.
Both doc-comment findings came from comments asserting another component's guarantees without checking that component's scope.

evidence: With maxAttempts<=0 the loop body never ran, and Recover returned Unconverged{Residual:""}, which contradicts the variant's documented contract. 7d8761a returns an error when maxAttempts < 1 and adds TestRecoverRejectsNonPositiveBudget.
guidance_note: When a sum-type variant promises a non-empty field, check every input that could reach that variant without filling the field (here, a zero loop budget) before opening the PR.

evidence: The original code always returned the generated backup name, even when moveAside was a no-op, and used an unpadded %d that breaks newestBackup's lexical-is-chronological ordering. 7d8761a fixes both, but it did not update the CLI consumer of Backup (see F6) or tighten the recognizer to the new width (see F10).
guidance_note: When a fix changes a returned field's contract (Backup can now be empty), grep every reader of that field and update them in the same commit.

evidence: runAttempt turned every RebuildCandidate error, including MkdirTemp and store I/O failures, into retry feedback. 7d8761a tags applier rejections with ErrInvalidMapping and returns all other errors as hard errors. The reply-hint says pushback, but the reply accepts the finding.
guidance_note: When an error is converted into retry feedback, first classify which errors the retry can actually fix, and tag only those.

evidence: newestBackup accepted any directory entry whose name started with the prefix. 7d8761a added e.IsDir() but still accepted any suffix, a gap the reviewer flagged as F10.
guidance_note: A recognizer for files a producer writes should match the producer's exact output shape (prefix + 19 digits) from the start, not just one property of it.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: `defer o.Candidate.Discard()` in promoteReconciled comes from the original commit, and 7d8761a did not touch internal/cli/lifeboat.go. The silently dropped Discard error was a real problem, and 61ce9b4 joins it into the return.
guidance_note: Never write a bare `defer x.Close()`-style cleanup whose error is dropped; this PR's own RequiresDrop branch already joined the Discard error.

evidence: F2's fix (7d8761a) made PromotionResult.Backup empty when nothing pre-existed, but the CLI still printed 'previous contents preserved at %s', which now shows a blank path. 8751cc2 made the clause conditional, a display fix that types-are-the-program does not describe.
guidance_note: When changing a struct field to be sometimes empty, grep its consumers (here the one Fprintf in lifeboat.go) and update them in the same fix commit.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 8751cc2 only changed the CLI print, and Recover's argument handling is original code. The empty-path half is real (filepath.Dir("") stages scratch under '.') and was fixed through a shared validateDoltRootDir. The nil-mapper half asks for a guard on a code-supplied function value, and declining it was correct.
guidance_note: When a new exported function takes a filesystem path, route it through the existing path validator (validateOpenArgs already checked empty paths) when writing it.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: PromoteCandidate's preamble is original code, and 8751cc2 did not touch promote.go. The empty-path validation was a real gap and was fixed. The nil cand guard was rightly declined because RebuildCandidate never returns (nil, nil).
guidance_note: When a new exported function takes a filesystem path, route it through the existing path validator when writing it.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: HealWorkspace is original code that 8751cc2 did not touch. With an empty path, LockWorkspaceExclusive would create the lock file in the working directory. bc1d499 applies the shared validateDoltRootDir here as well.
guidance_note: When a new exported function takes a filesystem path, route it through the existing path validator when writing it.

evidence: bc1d499, the named commit, did not touch newestBackup. The real cause is F4's fix (7d8761a), which added only e.IsDir() and left strings.HasPrefix accepting names like dolt.backup-manual, even though the same commit introduced the %019d stamp. cae1c9f adds isPromotionBackup with a shared promotionStampWidth constant.
guidance_note: When fixing one wrong input to a recognizer, write out every shape the producer can and cannot emit and reject all the non-produced shapes in the same fix.

evidence: The dump is taken under a shared hold and promotion happens later under an exclusive lock, so a commit made in between would be swapped out of the live workspace. The agent filed links-recovery-j0vl.7 because the fix is a design choice; PR #161 later closed the window with a head check at promote time. The flag is a false positive because the CLI sequence is original code.
guidance_note: When a multi-step operation reads under a shared lock and later writes under an exclusive one, design the read-to-write consistency check before opening the PR.

evidence: bc1d499, the fix for F7/F8/F9, added a comment claiming validateDoltRootDir is 'shared by every exported store entry point', while OpenSync still inlined its own empty-path check. cae1c9f routed OpenSync through validateOpenArgs, which made the comment true.
guidance_note: Before extracting a 'single enforcer' and saying so in a comment, grep for every inline copy of the check being replaced (here `strings.TrimSpace(doltRootDir) == ""`) and route them all through it.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: detachForPromotion dates from the original commit, and cae1c9f did not touch candidate.go. Discard clears c.root, so filepath.Join("", "workspace") returning a relative path is a reachable state. 7999dac rejects an empty root.
guidance_note: When a method's receiver has a consumed state (root cleared by Discard), check what each other method does in that state when writing it.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 7999dac only added the empty-root check, and the stamp has been time.Now().UnixNano() since the original code. A UnixNano repeat across two lock-serialized promotions is improbable, and the agent's 'clobber' framing overstates it because renaming onto an existing directory fails rather than overwriting. The uniqueBackupPath probe is still a cheap fix under the held lock.

The flag is a false positive: d3dd35b only added uniqueBackupPath, and Recover's `parentDir := filepath.Dir(canonicalDoltDir)` is original code. filepath.Dir("/path/dolt/") returns "/path/dolt", so candidates would be staged inside the canonical directory. 9344ac6 has validateDoltRootDir return filepath.Clean(path).
guidance_note: When adding a path validator for exported entry points (bc1d499), have it return the canonical form (filepath.Clean) rather than only reject empty input, so each caller derives its paths from one normalized value.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: PromoteCandidate's use of the unnormalized path is pre-review, and d3dd35b did not change it. A trailing separator turns '%s.backup-' into '/path/dolt/.backup-...', placing the backup inside the canonical directory. 9344ac6 normalizes the path.
guidance_note: Normalize path arguments once at the validation boundary and derive every lock, backup, and rename path from the normalized value.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: HealWorkspace's path handling is pre-review. With a trailing slash, newestBackup's filepath.Dir points at the canonical directory itself while filepath.Base strips the slash, so the backup scan looks in the wrong directory. 9344ac6 normalizes the path.
guidance_note: Normalize path arguments once at the validation boundary.

narrative: This PR took nine rounds. Three findings came from incomplete earlier fixes: F2 changed Backup to be sometimes empty but left the CLI printing it (F6); F4 filtered backups to directories but not to the producer's stamp shape (F10); and the shared path validator from F7 shipped with a comment claiming coverage OpenSync didn't have (F12). Most ON-POST-REVIEW flags were false positives: the reviewer kept finding unguarded edges of the original exported API (empty path, empty root, trailing slash, the concurrency window), one per round. Only round 2 consisted solely of fix-caused findings; F11 was handled correctly as a filed design followup that PR #161 later implemented.
guidance_observations: The exported recovery API shipped without a pass over its argument edges (empty, trailing-separator, consumed-receiver), so the reviewer found them one round at a time across rounds 3 to 7.
The agent posted three identical replies to each of F15, F16, and F17, as well as to their duplicate threads, which adds noise without information.

When fixing F7, the agent swept the empty-path check across all three exported functions at once, which kept that gap from recurring per function; the same sweep should have included path normalization.

evidence: RawDump gained a new dolt_head field, so a dump artifact produced before the field existed decodes with an empty head, and verifyHeadUnchanged would report it as ErrWorkspaceAdvanced with the message 'rebuilt from  but live is now at'. 25b3c37 adds a separate ErrMissingDumpProvenance and a test asserting the two errors stay distinct.
guidance_note: When adding a field to a persisted artifact, decide in the same change what an artifact missing that field means, and give that state its own error.

evidence: exec.Command("cp", "-a", ...) does tie the test to a platform binary. The reviewer's suggested cure (LookPath plus skip) would silently drop the core assertion on platforms without cp. The agent replaced the shell-out with a pure-Go copyTree, which keeps the diagnosis and rejects the skip.
guidance_note: In test helpers, write file copies in Go rather than shelling out to platform tools.

narrative: This PR closes the lost-update window deferred from #160/F11. Both round-0 findings were real; the agent fixed the missing-provenance state with a dedicated error and replaced the cp shell-out with a Go copy instead of the suggested skip. Round 1 was clean.
guidance_observations: The agent correctly rejected the reviewer's skip-the-assertion cure while keeping its diagnosis.

evidence: docs/agent-setup.md still said `git clone https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/links-issue-tracker`. The agent explained that the file was untracked when the `git grep -l | sed` rename ran, so the substitution skipped it.
guidance_note: After a bulk rename done with `git grep | sed`, run a plain `grep -r` over the whole working tree, untracked files included, before committing.

narrative: This is a docs and org-move PR with one finding: a stale clone URL in a new file that the tracked-files-only rename missed. It was fixed immediately and round 1 was clean.
guidance_observations: The miss came from the rename tool's scope (git grep sees only tracked files), and a final whole-tree grep would have caught it.

evidence: json.Unmarshal into mappingWire silently drops unknown keys, so a typo like 'prov' would only surface downstream as an unaccounted-for column. adeff95 switched to a Decoder with DisallowUnknownFields. That switch also changed the trailing-bytes behavior when UnmarshalJSON is called directly, which led to F3 through F5. The reply-hint says pushback, but the agent accepted.
guidance_note: When swapping json.Unmarshal for a json.Decoder, the Decoder stops checking that only one document is present, so either keep json.Unmarshal (with a strict wire type) or check for trailing data in the same commit.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: adeff95 only changed shapemap_json.go, and the bare `return nil, err` from os.ReadFile in recoverMapper is original code. Wrapping it matches the repo's 'read import spec: %w' convention.
guidance_note: Follow the repo's error-wrapping convention for file reads at the time you write the read.

evidence: The reviewer claimed a concatenated mapping file 'would currently be accepted', but the agent's own test says json.Unmarshal rejects it in its outer scan, and recoverMapper reads files through json.Unmarshal, so no production path accepted trailing data. The gap existed only for direct UnmarshalJSON calls, which F1's Decoder switch had opened. Adding a guard for that unreachable path led to two more findings (F4, F5).
guidance_note: Before accepting a 'this input is accepted' finding, check the actual call path (here json.Unmarshal's outer scan already rejects trailing data) and push back if production never reaches the gap.

evidence: The reviewer asked for a regression test for the trailing-data guard requested in F3. Once the guard existed, testing it was correct, and the agent's test documents that json.Unmarshal already rejected the input. The finding exists only because of F1's Decoder switch and the F3 guard.
guidance_note: Add a regression test in the same commit as any new decode guard.

evidence: F3's fix (2f236c7) wrote `if err := dec.Decode(new(json.RawMessage)); err != io.EOF { return fmt.Errorf("...trailing data...") }`, which throws away the encoding/json syntax error and its location for unparseable trailing bytes. f5ca0d8 made it a three-way switch that wraps the non-nil, non-EOF error.
guidance_note: When a guard replaces an error with a new message, list the error's possible values (EOF, nil, syntax error) and wrap every one that carries information.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: f5ca0d8 only touched shapemap_json.go, and the success line printed only as human text dates from #160. ada9101 routes it through printValue with a recoverResult payload. It reads a local fs.Bool("json") rather than outputModeFromWriter, and the packet does not show whether the global --json reaches this command that way.
guidance_note: When adding a CLI command, route its output through the dual-mode printValue and read the global output mode, the way sibling commands do.

evidence: F6's fix (ada9101) added the --json flag but left the usage string as 'usage: lit lifeboat recover [--mapping <file>]', which omits it.
guidance_note: When adding a flag, update the command's usage string in the same commit.

narrative: This PR took seven rounds, and three of them (rounds 2, 3, and 5) contained only fix-caused findings. F1's switch to a strict Decoder gave up the single-document check when UnmarshalJSON is called directly. The reviewer flagged this as a production gap, and the agent accepted it even though its own test showed json.Unmarshal already rejects the input. The guard it added then dropped the underlying syntax error (F5). Separately, adding --json (F6) left the usage string stale (F7).
guidance_observations: The agent accepted F3 even though the test it wrote stated the premise did not hold for the production json.Unmarshal path; a quick check of the call path would have prevented two rounds.
Small fixes were pushed one round at a time; each fix commit was not checked for the same class of drift (usage text, wrapped errors) before pushing.

evidence: sortEmitters compared only Collection and then field names, and sort.Slice is not stable, so two same-collection emitters with the same field names could swap places and give one mapping two encodings. The fix keys on each emitter's full identity and is locked by TestShapeMappingJSONStableOrderMultiEmitter.
guidance_note: A canonical encoder's sort key must cover every field of the item's identity; otherwise use sort.SliceStable over a deterministic input order.

narrative: This is a large fan-out redesign with one finding: a partial sort key that broke the stable-encoding guarantee. The agent fixed it with a total key and a test, and round 1 was clean.

evidence: The test comment said '(honest: those migrations really did run)', while the fixture writes the ahead row directly with stampGooseVersionAhead. The agent reworded the comment to separate what the field means in production from what the fixture does.
guidance_note: Test comments should describe what the fixture actually builds, not what the production state it imitates would mean.

narrative: This PR got one comment-accuracy nit on a test, which was fixed in one round, and round 1 was clean.

evidence: The test name ends in '...AndArchived', but the hunk only exercises a container reopen and a leaf start, and no archived issue reaches applyTransition. The agent added an archive followed by an assertion that applyTransition(archived, close) is refused.
guidance_note: When extracting a guard into a helper, write one test case per branch of the guard, and name the test after the cases it actually asserts.

narrative: This PR had one finding: a test whose name promised coverage of the archived guard that it lacked. The agent added the missing case, and round 1 was clean.
